items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: I had the 'sweet' trio, 'sweet' in quotes and that is Johnny Fulton, Skin Young and Charlie Gaylord

ctx.x: That was our record, and then they gave me a tune by the name of "Changes," a Walter Donaldson tune, awfully nice.

It turned out well. I used all the voices in there. I went to Paul and asked him, I said, 'What do I use or what don't I use?' 'Use whatever you want.' So boy I did. I had everybody and I had the 'sweet' trio, 'sweet' in quotes and that is Johnny Fulton, Skin Young and Charlie Gaylord and then I put let's see, I put Rinker in with them because he could sing a falsetto and I had Bing sing -- he sang the patter. That worked out great, and Steve, of course, spanked his bass on the Beiderbecke part of it, and the…

It turned out good and so did the other record, the Washboard and that and I was off to a good start, so in the meantime I'm working out a couple arrangements with like Tommy and Jimmy, trying to get them set in what they like to do. One night out in Chicago, we played three different theatres in Chicago and one night uptown, or downtown, I don't know what it was. It was near the outside of the city, Tommy comes down and says, 'I'm going to quit.' 'What? Gee, we're just getting started. What are you going to do?'
